transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02 15:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood); Omar Reyes (Redwood CSM); Daniel Rivers, Sofia Martinez, Liam O'Connor, Priya Gupta (Stationhouse)

Summary:
Quick activation kickoff for a 6-week pilot focused on customer service LLM assistant; main goals: confirm pilot success criteria, surface security/SSO/VPC constraints, agree on telemetry and cost targets, and schedule benchmarks for model/latency evaluation.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros then we'll run through the proposed pilot plan. Sorry slight echo—I'm on a headset.
[00:22] Daniel Rivers: Hey Alex, Daniel here. We're excited to get moving, we've got a small infra team and the ML folks lined up.
[00:31] Sofia Martinez: Sofia, VP Eng. We're mainly focused on production readiness and SLA needs.
[00:37] Liam O'Connor: Liam, security. We'll be watching encryption, KMS and audit trail stuff.
[00:42] Priya Gupta: Priya, SRE, hi all.
[00:45] Priya Nair (Redwood): Hi all — quick background: Redwood's pilot template usually runs 4–6 weeks; we do initial validation on hosted, then if needed spin up Dedicated or Private for isolation. We'll adapt to Stationhouse constraints.
[01:03] Alex Chen: Agenda — confirm success metrics (latency P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, quality on our eval prompt set), security gating (SOC2/ audit logs / SSO), and sample traffic. Also who owns what on your side.
[01:22] Daniel Rivers: For success, our product team wants P95 under 350ms for short chat-turns and under 1s for longer document ops. Cost target is roughly 40% less than our current in-house serving. Quality: maintain or exceed current approx 87% helpfulness on our evals.
[01:46] Omar Reyes: Got it. We'll map that to model choices. Quick note, sometimes transcripts show Redwood product names oddly — the engineer might say K-V cash instead of KV cache — just flagging typical ASR noise.
[01:58] Liam O'Connor: On security: we need SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, per-tenant RBAC and audit logs retained for 13 months minimum. Also, data at rest must be encrypted with our KMS and key rotation support.
[02:19] Alex Chen: That's expected — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit log exports. We'll attach the compliance pack after the call.
[02:29] Sofia Martinez: Are there any gotchas with Dedicated vs Private? We prefer Dedicated for cost predictability but worried about data leaking to multi-tenant systems.
[02:40] Priya Nair: Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and tenancy isolation, but Private gives total network control (VPC and on-prem). For many finance customers Dedicated with strict tenancy is sufficient; we'll show the tenancy diagram.
[02:58] Daniel Rivers: Timeline: we want pilot in QA by Nov 15 and production ramp in early January if pilot goes well. Is that realistic?
[03:07] Alex Chen: It's tight but doable. We need your prompt sets and traffic histogram this week, plus SSO app configuration details. We'll prioritize the benchmark and can run hosted baseline in 48 hours after we get samples.
[03:21] Priya Gupta: On-network side, we can't open public egress from prod. Is Redwood able to connect over a VPC peering or PrivateLink?
[03:31] Priya Nair: Yes — we support VPC peering and PrivateLink; we'll capture the CIDR and necessary ports. For hosted baseline we'd need at least a staging path that can call Redwood's endpoints.
[03:47] Sofia Martinez: Observability — what level of telemetry do we get? Token-level cost, tracing, per-route latency?
[03:55] Omar Reyes: You get token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and traces that can stitch across your request IDs. We can also ship sample logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders.
[04:10] Daniel Rivers: Great. On model selection: we run a mix of short chat and longer summarization. Do you have recommendations?
[04:18] Priya Nair: For hybrid workloads we usually recommend a smaller lower-latency variant for short-turn chat and an L larger for summarization, with automated routing and fallback. We can quantize to reduce cost. We'll propose three candidate models in the runbook.
[04:34] Sofia Martinez: Any concerns re hallucinations or regression monitoring during the pilot?
[04:39] Alex Chen: We'll set up quality monitoring tied to your prompt sets and send regression alerts. Also suggest a manual eval cadence — weekly checks during pilot.
[04:49] Liam O'Connor: On compliance: can we get a SOC2 attestation and details on where logs are stored?
[04:55] Omar Reyes: Yes — we'll share SOC2 docs and a log retention map. Logs for hosted are stored in our secure bucket in the region you choose; Private gives you customer managed storage.
[05:09] Daniel Rivers: Pricing — need an estimate for a 6-week pilot with 100k tokens/day average; and price for Dedicated reserve options.
[05:19] Alex Chen: We'll send an initial pilot estimate today and a Dedicated tier pricing sheet. Note that batching and prefix caching can reduce per-token cost; we can estimate with your histogram.
[05:32] Priya Gupta: About encryption — key rotation, HSM or bring-your-own-key?
[05:36] Priya Nair: We support BYOK via KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys in Private deployments. We'll put the KMS integration doc in the follow-up.
[05:50] Sofia Martinez: Ok next steps recap?
[05:53] Alex Chen: Recap: 1) Redwood: send runbook, SSO/SAML guide, SOC2 and compliance pack, and pilot pricing by Nov 5. 2) Stationhouse: upload prompt sets + traffic profile by Nov 9. 3) Redwood SE to run hosted baseline benchmark (50k tokens) and share latency/cost spreadsheet by Nov 6. We'll set a follow up with finance for Dedicated pricing on Nov 12.
[06:15] Daniel Rivers: Sounds good. Also can we set up a 2-hour deep-dive with your SEs next week for network/Private deployment specifics?
[06:24] Omar Reyes: Yes let's schedule, I'll propose slots.
[06:28] (crosstalk)
[06:30] Priya Nair: Quick technical note: for performance tests please include real prompt lengths; synthetic short prompts will overstate throughput. Also include KV cache warmup patterns — long-running chat sessions benefit from cache priming.
[06:46] Daniel Rivers: Noted.
[06:48] Sofia Martinez: One more question — if we see a quality regression after rollout what's the rollback path?
[06:54] Alex Chen: We have rollback/fallback flows — automatic fallback to a verified model variant and can route traffic to a lower-capacity but proven model. Also can pin client to prior model for a percentage of traffic while doing A/B. We'll include the rollout policy in the runbook.
[07:12] Priya Gupta: Network checklist — we'll need IP ranges and cert exchange details.
[07:17] Priya Nair: We'll put a short network appendix in the runbook.
[07:21] Daniel Rivers: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[07:24] Alex Chen: None on our side; just awaiting your prompt set and the SSO app metadata.
[07:29] (pause)
[07:33] Sofia Martinez: Quick note on stakeholders — can Redwood include a short one-pager for procurement about billing cadence for pilots vs Dedicated reserves? Our procurement team needs that when we talk to finance.
[07:43] Omar Reyes: We'll include a procurement one-pager in the follow-up.
[07:46] Alex Chen: Ok we'll circulate materials by Thursday. Thanks everyone.
[07:52] Daniel Rivers: Thanks, talk soon.

Meeting close and recorded at 15:47 PT.

Artifacts referenced:
- Pilot runbook (to be shared)
- SSO/SAML integration guide (to be shared)
- SOC2 + compliance pack (to be shared)
- Latency/cost benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared)

Notes on transcript accuracy: ASR occasionally mislabels acronyms (K-V cash/KV cache), and sometimes swaps product names — manual review recommended for legal docs.
